disclaimer: This report is an automated engineering quality indication produced by a prototype. A PASS result means only that the listed tools reported no findings above the policy thresholds for the assessed scope. It is NOT a security certification, does NOT establish ISO 26262 / ISO 21434 / ASPICE compliance, and is NOT an Audi IT or release approval. Checks marked NOT EXECUTED or NOT APPLICABLE provide no assurance.

categories.title: Broken Access Control
categories.aspect: PostgreSQL row level security, grants and policies in SQL files; unauthenticated operations in OpenAPI documents; CORS wildcards
categories.not_covered: Authorisation logic in application code; object-level access checks; anything decided at runtime

categories.title: Cryptographic Failures
categories.aspect: Weak hash/cipher use in Python; disabled TLS verification; unverified JWTs; plain-http endpoints in API and MCP configuration
categories.not_covered: Key management, data-at-rest encryption, protocol configuration of deployed systems; C/C++ cryptography

categories.title: Injection
categories.aspect: Known injection sinks: shell, eval, SQL string building, format strings, dynamic SQL, unsafe HTML
categories.not_covered: Data-flow across files or services; whether a flagged sink is reachable with untrusted data

categories.title: Insecure Design
categories.aspect: Existence of a specification, architecture documentation and a threat model
categories.not_covered: Whether the design is secure. No tool evaluates this; it needs review

categories.title: Security Misconfiguration
categories.aspect: Debug/bind-all settings, CORS, permissive database grants, API and MCP configuration files in the repository
categories.not_covered: Configuration of deployed infrastructure, cloud resources, containers, headers at runtime

categories.title: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
categories.aspect: Pinned/locked dependencies; known advisories for pip, npm and Bun lockfiles (needs --allow-network)
categories.not_covered: C/C++ and vendored dependencies, container base images, yarn/pnpm/Poetry/uv lockfiles, licence compliance

categories.title: Identification and Authentication Failures
categories.aspect: Hardcoded credentials and key files; credentials in MCP configuration; missing or weak security schemes in OpenAPI documents
categories.not_covered: Session handling, password policy, MFA, token lifetime, the authentication implementation itself

categories.title: Software and Data Integrity Failures
categories.aspect: Unsafe deserialisation; unpinned packages launched by MCP configuration; lockfiles; presence of a CI pipeline
categories.not_covered: Build pipeline integrity, artefact signing, update mechanisms

categories.title: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
categories.not_covered: Not assessed at Level 1

categories.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
categories.not_covered: Not assessed at Level 1 (needs data-flow analysis)

categories.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
categories.aspect: Only where authorisation is implemented as PostgreSQL row level security in SQL files
categories.not_covered: Object-level checks in API handlers

categories.title: Broken Authentication
categories.aspect: Operations without a security requirement in the OpenAPI document; disabled JWT verification; hardcoded credentials
categories.not_covered: The authentication implementation; endpoints that are not in an OpenAPI document

categories.title: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
categories.not_covered: Not assessed at Level 1

categories.title: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
categories.aspect: Whether the OpenAPI document mentions rate limiting (HTTP 429) at all
categories.not_covered: Actual rate limits, payload limits, timeouts, cost controls

categories.title: Broken Function Level Authorization
categories.aspect: Operations without a security requirement in the OpenAPI document
categories.not_covered: Role checks in handlers; admin functions not described in the document

categories.title: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
categories.not_covered: Not assessable by static tools

categories.title: Server Side Request Forgery
categories.not_covered: Not assessed at Level 1

categories.title: Security Misconfiguration
categories.aspect: Plain-http servers in the OpenAPI document; CORS wildcards; disabled TLS verification; debug/bind-all settings
categories.not_covered: Deployed gateway, TLS and header configuration

categories.title: Improper Inventory Management

categories.not_covered: Whether the contract matches the deployed API; old versions still running

checks.title: Contribution and review process is defined

findings.message: Not found: Contribution and review process is defined. Looked for: contributing*, docs/contributing*, .github/pull_request_template*, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/*, codeowners, .github/codeowners, docs/codeowners, .gitlab/merge_request_templates/* ...
findings.guidance: Generated code needs the same review as hand-written code. A defined process (who reviews, what must be true before merge) is what makes that enforceable. Add CONTRIBUTING.md (branching, commit and review rules, definition of done), a pull request template with a checklist (spec updated, tests added, EAF run attached) and a CODEOWNERS file.

checks.title: Security policy or threat model is documented

findings.message: Not found: Security policy or threat model is documented. Looked for: security.md, .github/security.md, docs/security*, docs/threat*, threat-model*, docs/tara*
findings.guidance: IT security reviewers ask first how vulnerabilities are reported and which threats were considered. Without a document the answer is 'none'. Add SECURITY.md (how to report a vulnerability, supported versions) and, for anything networked, a short threat model: assets, entry points, trust boundaries, and the mitigations you rely on.

limitations: Level 1 inspects source text only: nothing is built, executed or tested.
A PASS reflects the configured tools and thresholds only; absence of findings is not absence of defects.
Engineering-practice checks establish that a document exists and has minimal substance. They do not judge whether it is correct, complete or followed.
Standards coverage is partial by construction: a mapped category means some checks look for instances of that weakness class, not that the category is satisfied.
